lesson.text: Quick memory: in an invasion game, what is a free player? (A teammate with no defender close by, so it is safe to pass to them.) Today: team tactics.
A tactic is a plan to help your team win. Teams plan how to attack: keep the ball, find space and score. And they plan how to defend: stop the other team scoring, and win the ball back.

Positions and roles: in football, a goalkeeper guards the goal, defenders stop attacks, midfielders link defence and attack, and attackers try to score. Each player knows their job, and helps the others.
Netball has 7 players, each with a bib: GS, GA, WA, C, WD, GD and GK. Each may only go in some thirds of the court. Only the Goal Shooter and Goal Attack may score, from inside the shooting circle.
Attacking tactics: spread out to make the pitch big, and pass to a free teammate. Two attackers against one defender is an overload: run at the defender, and pass the moment they come to you.
Defending tactics: make the pitch small by staying close together, stay goal-side, between the attacker and your goal, and block the passing lanes. Mark a player each, or guard an area each: a zone.
A one-two (a give and go): pass to a teammate, run past your defender into space, and get the ball straight back. When your team loses the ball, everyone switches to defending at once.
Try it in the world: build a pitch and plan a 3 against 3 game with friends. Choose a tactic before you play, then ask afterwards: did it work, and what will we change?

exercises.hint: Teams choose one before a game, and change it if it does not work.
choices: a plan to help your team win
exercises.explain: A tactic is a plan to help your team win, in attack and in defence.

exercises.prompt: When your team loses the ball, everyone should switch to defending.
exercises.hint: Who has the ball now, and what will they try to do?
exercises.explain: True: the moment the other team has the ball, your whole team defends.

exercises.prompt: In netball, which two positions may score a goal?
exercises.hint: Which positions have 'Goal' and attack in their names?
exercises.explain: The Goal Shooter (GS) and the Goal Attack (GA), from inside the shooting circle.

exercises.prompt: Match each football position to its job.
exercises.hint: Think of where each player stands on the pitch.
exercises.explain: The goalkeeper guards the goal, defenders stop attacks, midfielders link the two, and attackers try to score.

exercises.prompt: Your team is attacking. Should you spread out or bunch together?
exercises.hint: Which makes more space to pass into?
choices: spread out, to make the pitch big
exercises.explain: Spread out: a big pitch gives your team space and pulls the defenders apart.

exercises.prompt: Your team is defending. How should you play?
exercises.hint: Where must the attackers get to, and how can you make it hard?
choices: spread out along the side lines
all wait on the halfway line
all chase the ball at once
exercises.explain: Stay close together and goal-side: there is little space to pass or run through.

exercises.prompt: Put a one-two (a give and go) in order.
items: you have the ball in space
your teammate passes it straight back
run past the defender into space
exercises.explain: Pass, run past the defender, get the ball straight back, and you are in space.

exercises.prompt: In player-to-player marking, each defender guards one attacker.
exercises.hint: Who does each defender stay with?
exercises.explain: True: each defender marks one attacker. In a zone, each guards an area instead.

exercises.hint: Which ones help your team when it has the ball?
exercises.explain: Attacking: spreading out, the one-two, making the pitch big. Defending: goal-side, blocking lanes, a zone.

choices: more attackers than defenders in one area
too many players on the pitch
exercises.explain: An overload is more attackers than defenders in one part of the pitch, like 2 against 1.

exercises.prompt: Two attackers face one defender. The attacker with the ball should …
exercises.hint: How can you make the defender choose which attacker to stop?
choices: run at the defender, then pass
exercises.explain: Run at the defender to draw them in, then pass to your free teammate.

exercises.prompt: Blue is attacking, but everyone is bunched together. What should blue do?
exercises.hint: Look at the empty parts of the pitch.
choices: spread out into the empty space
move even closer to the ball
exercises.explain: Spread out: the right side of the pitch is empty, and a teammate there would be free.

exercises.prompt: In a zone defence, each defender guards an area of the pitch, not one player.
exercises.hint: What does the word zone mean?
exercises.explain: True: each defender guards a zone, an area, and marks whoever comes into it.

exercises.prompt: The other team is very fast. Which tactic might help most?
exercises.hint: Fast players are hard to stop when there is lots of space behind you.
choices: stay close together near your goal
mark them all on the halfway line
exercises.explain: Stay compact near your goal: there is little space behind you for fast players to run into.

exercises.prompt: A 5-a-side football team has a goalkeeper, 2 defenders and 1 midfielder. How many attackers does it have?
exercises.hint: 5 players in all: take away the ones you know.

exercises.prompt: Your team wins the ball back. Put what happens next in order.
exercises.hint: First you need to see who is free.
items: look up for a free teammate
exercises.explain: Look up, pass to a free teammate, spread out and move forward, then attack the goal.
